heard: A single blinking star once destroyed the entire known universe. In 1920, astronomer Harlow Shapley argued the Milky Way was the only galaxy in existence. Heber Curtis countered that fuzzy spiral clouds were actually distant, independent island universes. In October 1923, Edwin Hubble used the 100-inch Hooker telescope to photograph the Andromeda Nebula. He spotted a changing star, V-1, that proved Andromeda was roughly one million light years away. That distance was far outside the Milky Way, instantly making the cosmos billions of times larger. Shapley read Hubble's letter and told a colleague, here is the letter that destroyed my universe. Everything we knew about our home changed because a single blinking star once destroyed the entire known universe.
